inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: The project is a simulation environment benchmark built with the Gym API and Drake simulations for a Franka Panda
BaseDrakeRobotEnv derives from gym.Env, so every Fleet-Tools environment uses the legacy Gym API
FrankaDrakeEnv derives from BaseDrakeRobotEnv and is constructed from a task_config
The action space is PandaTaskSpace6D(task_config.env.action_scale), a 6-element end-effector delta
PandaTaskSpace6D returns a Box of shape [6] with the first three bounds +-trans_scale and the last three +-rotation_scale
The Hammer teleop task configuration sets action_scale [0.04, 0.4] and numObservations [9]
The observation space is Box(low=-1.0, high=1.0) with shape numObservations
DrakeBaseConfig sets numActions to 6 and numObservations to [10, 240, 320]
DrakeBaseConfig sets the simulation dt to 0.004 s and substep_num to 40
The environment control period env_dt is sim_dt multiplied by substep_num
step computes the reward with _get_reward and returns the legacy four-tuple obs, reward, done, info
step sets done to sim_done, so the base environment has no separate time limit in step
reset returns the legacy four-tuple obs, reward, done, info
seed uses gym.utils.seeding.np_random and Drake's RandomGenerator and returns [seed]
The environment is registered under the id FrankaDrakeEnv-v0

determinism.notes: the fake draws its initial observation from random.Random(seed) and is otherwise deterministic; upstream seeds gym's np_random and Drake's RandomGenerator, so one seed does not give the same trajectory on the two

gaps: the fake is a deterministic 9-value observation and 6-value action stand-in, not the Drake contact simulation: no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, controller, rendering or sensors are modelled

the upstream default DrakeBaseConfig uses a [10, 240, 320] image observation; the package fake uses the Hammer teleop configuration's 9-value keypoint observation instead, because the standard bridge carries only JSON values
the base reward is 0; the knife, spatula, hammer and wrench task rewards are not modelled
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
the upstream environment was never opened here (it needs a Hydra task_config, pydrake, torch and the bundled assets) and no upstream trajectory was compared with the fake
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
